Case_17013/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Figure 1a. Coronal section of CT abdomen. Arrows indicate two large hypoechoic liver lesions; the regular walls are consistent with cystic lesions. Also indicated: a large cystic lesion in the small bowel mesentery.

description.short_caption: Coronal CT of the abdomen showing large hypodense cystic lesions in the liver and mesentery.
description.detailed_description: This coronal CT image of the abdomen reveals two large hypodense lesions in the liver, consistent with cystic lesions, as indicated by arrows. The lesions have regular, well-defined walls. Additionally, a large cystic lesion is visible in the small bowel mesentery, also marked by an arrow. The image demonstrates good contrast resolution, allowing clear visualization of the lesions against the surrounding tissues.
visible_findings: Two large hypodense cystic lesions in the liver with regular walls.
A large cystic lesion in the small bowel mesentery.
Arrows marking the lesions for emphasis.

Case_17013/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Microscopic features of the ruptured mesenteric cyst (at low power) demonstrating multiple layers of parasite-derived cyst wall

description.short_caption: CT scan showing a large mesenteric cyst in the abdomen.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the abdomen demonstrates a large, well-defined cystic lesion in the mesentery, measuring 6.7 x 10 x 8.5 cm as indicated by the annotation. The cyst appears to have thin walls and is likely fluid-filled, with no evidence of calcification or solid components. Surrounding abdominal structures are displaced but not invaded, consistent with a benign process. The image does not directly show microscopic features of the cyst wall.
visible_findings: large cystic lesion in the mesentery

Case_17013/figure5.jpg.source_caption: Microscopic features of the ruptured mesenteric cyst (at low power) demonstrating multiple layers of parasite-derived cyst wall

description.short_caption: Low-power histopathology of a ruptured mesenteric cyst showing parasite-derived multilayered cyst wall.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image, captured at low magnification, shows a ruptured mesenteric cyst with distinct multilayered structures. The cyst wall exhibits concentric layers of varying thickness, consistent with parasite-derived material. The image highlights the structural complexity of the cyst wall, which may include laminated layers and fibrous components. No cellular infiltrates or surrounding tissue are prominently visible at this magnification.

Case_17013/figure6.jpg.source_caption: CT abdomen at 7 months of follow- up demonstrating compromised integrity of the cyst consistent with transitional phase

description.short_caption: Histopathology showing the cyst wall with transitional phase changes.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a section of a cyst wall stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The wall demonstrates a layered structure with cellular components and a transition zone. The integrity of the cyst wall appears compromised, with evidence of inflammatory infiltrates and possible degeneration. The image provides microscopic details consistent with a transitional phase of cyst evolution.
visible_findings: compromised integrity of the cyst wall

Case_17013/figure7.jpg.source_caption: PAIR (Puncture-Aspiration–Injection–Re-aspiration) of the right hepatic lobe cyst via CT guidance

description.short_caption: PAIR procedure of a hepatic cyst under CT guidance.
description.detailed_description: The image consists of two axial CT scans of the abdomen. The left panel shows a large, well-defined cystic lesion in the right hepatic lobe, consistent with a hepatic cyst. The right panel demonstrates the PAIR procedure in progress, with a needle inserted into the cyst under CT guidance. The cyst appears partially decompressed, and there is evidence of injected material or aspiration. The scans are non-contrast, and the needle trajectory is clearly visualized.
visible_findings: large cystic lesion in the right hepatic lobe
needle inserted into the cyst under CT guidance
evidence of injected material or aspiration

Case_17013/figure8.jpg.source_caption: CT abdomen at 7 months of follow- up demonstrating compromised integrity of the cyst consistent with transitional phase

description.short_caption: CT abdomen showing a cyst with compromised integrity, consistent with a transitional phase.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the abdomen demonstrates a large cystic lesion in the upper abdomen. The cyst appears to have irregular margins and compromised integrity, with evidence of internal debris or partial collapse. Adjacent structures, including the liver and spleen, are visible. The findings are consistent with a transitional phase of a cystic lesion, potentially due to infection or degeneration.
visible_findings: large cystic lesion in the upper abdomen
internal debris or partial collapse of the cyst

Case_17013/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Macroscopic picture of ruptured mesenteric cyst

description.short_caption: Abdominal CT showing two large cystic lesions in the mesentery.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the abdomen shows two large, well-defined cystic lesions in the mesenteric region. The lesions are labeled with their respective dimensions: 4.9 x 5.8 x 5.4 cm and 7.7 x 8.6 x 8.3 cm. The cysts appear hypodense relative to surrounding tissues, with no clear evidence of internal septations or solid components. The surrounding abdominal structures are visible, and there is no obvious sign of rupture or leakage in this image.
visible_findings: two large cystic lesions in the mesentery
no visible internal septations or solid components
